questions.question: Which commando battalion is being raised by the Indian Army to strengthen swift strike capabilities along the borders with China and Pakistan?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bhairav.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__**

__
 
• **The Indian Army is raising the Bhairav__ commando battalions to enhance swift strike capabilities along the borders with __China__ and __Pakistan__.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Bhairav battalions__ are newly raised light commando units with ~__250 soldiers__ each, drawn from existing infantry battalions.**
 
• **These battalions aim to __boost swift strike capabilities__ along critical borders and relieve __Para-Special Forces__ for more high-risk missions.**
 
• **Each battalion is __equipped with advanced technology__ such as drones, surveillance systems, and modern weaponry.**
 
• **They will operate across diverse terrains, from __mountains__ to __deserts__, and conduct reconnaissance, interdiction, and disruption of enemy forces.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Unit Composition**__

 __
 
• Each Bhairav commando battalion will consist of ~250 soldiers__ and __7–8 officers__.
 
 
 
• __**Deployment Locations**__
 __
 
• Initial units will be located in areas like Leh__, __Srinagar__, __Nagrota__, and the __western desert sector__.
 
 
 
• __**Strategic Modernization**__
 __
 
• The Bhairav battalion is part of India’s ongoing military modernization drive, alongside Rudra brigades__ and __Divyastra batteries__.

questions.question: Which two wetlands have recently been designated as Ramsar sites in September 2025?

options.text: Keoladeo National Park and Sonepat Wetland

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Gokul Jalashaya and Udaipur Jheel.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__**

__
 
• **Two wetlands in Bihar, Gokul Jalashaya in Buxar and Udaipur Jheel in West Champaran, have been designated as Ramsar sites of international importance.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• **Gokul Jalashaya spans 448 hectares in Buxar district, while Udaipur Jheel covers 319 hectares in West Champaran district.**
 
• **With these additions, India now has a total of 94 Ramsar sites, covering 13,60,719 hectares nationwide.**
 
• **Ramsar sites are wetlands recognized under the Ramsar Convention for their international ecological importance.**
 
• **The Ramsar Convention is headquartered in Gland, Switzerland, and aims to conserve and sustainably use wetlands globally.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• Gokul Jalashaya__

 __
 
• Located in Buxar district, Bihar; significant for supporting biodiversity and wetland ecosystems.
 
 
 
• Udaipur Jheel__
 __
 
• Located in West Champaran district, Bihar; important for migratory birds and local hydrology.
 
 
 
• Ramsar Convention__
 __
 
• International treaty established in 1971 to conserve wetlands and promote sustainable use.
 
 
 
• India’s Wetlands Network__
 
 
• India now has 96 Ramsar sites, reflecting ongoing commitment to wetland conservation and biodiversity protection.

questions.question: Which food and dairy items were made GST-free under the new reforms?
questions.solution:
Correct Answer: __**B) UHT milk, paneer, chapati, khakra.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__**

__
 
• **GST 2.0 introduces a streamlined tax structure with two main slabs of 5% and 18%, along with a 40% demerit rate for sin and luxury goods**. The reforms emphasize tax reductions on essential items, healthcare, and automobiles. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__** 

__
 
• **GST Council Meeting:** 56th meeting under FM Nirmala Sitharaman with participation of 31 states and UTs.
 
• **New Structure**: **Two-slab GST** system of **5%** and** 18%**, with a **special 40% demerit rate for super-luxury and sin goods.**
 
• **Implementation Date**: All rate changes (except tobacco) effective from September 22, 2025 (Navratri’s first day).
 
• **GST-Free Items:** UHT milk, paneer, pizza bread, chapati, khakra, parathas, erasers.
 
• **Food & Daily Use Items:** Packaged food (juices, butter, cheese, pasta, nuts, sauces, chocolates, instant noodles, namkeens, coffee) now at 5%.
 
• **Household Goods: **Hair oil, soaps, shampoos, toothpaste, toothbrushes, bicycles, kitchenware, tableware → 5%.
 
• **Medical Relief: **Oxygen, gauze, bandages, diagnostic kits lowered to 5%; 33 lifesaving medicines fully exempted.
 
• **Healthcare Support**: Vision correction spectacles cut to 5% (from 28%).
 
• **Insurance**: Life and health insurance policies made GST-exempt.
 
• **Services**: Gyms, salons, barbers, yoga services reduced from 18% to 5%.
 
• **White Goods & Autos:**
 
 
• **ACs, TVs, dishwashers** → 18% (from 28%).
 
• **Small cars** (petrol ≤1200cc, diesel ≤1500cc), motorcycles ≤350cc, auto parts → 18%.
 
• **Luxury cars** → 40%.
 
• **EVs **remain at 5%.
 
• **Infrastructure**: Cement cut from 28% → 18%.
 
 
 
• **Sectoral Reforms:**
 
 
• **Textiles**: Manmade fibre (18% → 5%), yarn (12% → 5%).
 
• **Fertilisers**: Ammonia, sulphuric acid, nitric acid (18% → 5%).
 
 
 
• **Luxury/Sin Goods**: 40% GST slab includes pan masala, gutka, zarda, tobacco products, caffeinated beverages, yachts, helicopters, private-use airplanes, large motorcycles (>350cc).
 
• **Revenue Concerns:** States raised ₹80,000–1.5 lakh crore loss fears; Centre estimated net fiscal impact of ₹48,000 crore.
 
• **Industry Reaction:** CII and industry groups welcomed reforms; expected to ease compliance, reduce litigation, boost demand, and create jobs.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• GST 2.0 is the biggest overhaul since 2017.
 
• Corrects inverted duty structure in textiles and fertilisers.
 
• Rate rationalisation reduces slabs from 4 **(5%, 12%, 18%, 28%**) to 2 (**+ one demerit rate**).
 
• PM Modi welcomed the reforms as pro-people, benefiting farmers, MSMEs, middle-class, women, and youth.
 
• Sin goods (tobacco/pan masala) still under 28% + cess until state loan compensation is cleared.
 
• The reforms will directly reduce costs for households, farmers, and small industries.
 
• Expected to simplify compliance via automated refunds and registrations.
 
• Reforms seen as pathbreaking with potential to stimulate consumption and growth.

questions.question: According to the Air Quality Life Index (AQLI), which country is ranked as the second most polluted in the world?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**India.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__**

__
 
• **India is ranked as the second most polluted country in the world according to the Air Quality Life Index (AQLI).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• **India has the second-highest level of air pollution globally, reducing life expectancy by an average of 3.5 years due to severe air quality issues.**
 
• The AQLI is developed by Professor Michael Greenstone and the Energy Policy Institute at the University of Chicago (EPIC), offering hyper-local data on the impact of air pollution on life expectancy.
 
• **South Asia, including India, Bangladesh, Nepal, and Pakistan, remains the most polluted region in the world.**
 
• The report emphasizes the urgent need for evidence-based policies to reduce air pollution and improve public health.
 
• India’s air pollution level significantly impacts life expectancy, with some regions like Northern India losing up to 8.2 years of life due to severe air quality degradation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• Air Quality Life Index (AQLI):__ A measure developed to show how air pollution affects life expectancy by translating pollution levels into years of life lost.
 
• __Bangladesh:__ Currently ranked as the most polluted country globally, with air pollution levels 12 times higher than the WHO limits.
 
• __China:__ Has made significant progress in reducing pollution by 40.8% since 2014 through aggressive policies like cleaner heating and traffic restrictions.

questions.question: The eminent figure, Jagdeep Chhokar, passed away at 80 after a heart attack in September 2025. What was he famous for?

options.text: Founding the First State Ombudsman of India, and Pioneering the Lokayukta Movement in Maharashtra
Being a prominent Banker and founder of the GIFT City in Gujarat
Serving as the Chief Election Commissioner of India
Founding the Association for Democratic Reforms and advocating for electoral reforms

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Founding the Association for Democratic Reforms (ADR) and advocating for electoral reforms.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__**

__
 
• **Jagdeep Chhokar, co-founder of ADR, passed away at the age of 80 due to a heart attack.**
 
• **Chhokar was known for his dedication to increasing transparency in Indian politics and promoting electoral reforms.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• **Jagdeep Chhokar co-founded the Association for Democratic Reforms (ADR) in 1999 with the aim of increasing transparency in politics.**
 
• Chhokar was a strong advocate for electoral reforms and worked to make election processes more transparent and accountable.
 
• He played a significant role in pushing for Supreme Court judgments that mandated candidates to disclose criminal cases, finances, and educational background.
 
• Chhokar’s work with ADR contributed to landmark judgments, including the ruling against the electoral bond scheme in 2024 and the new system for verifying Electronic Voting Machines (EVMs).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• Association for Democratic Reforms (ADR)__

 __
 
• Founded in 1999, ADR is an organization that advocates for electoral reforms and greater transparency in politics.
 
• ADR has been instrumental in filing petitions that led to significant Supreme Court judgments regarding election disclosures and EVM verifications.
 
 
 
• Electoral Bond Scheme__
 __
 
• The electoral bond scheme was introduced to fund political parties, but it was ruled unconstitutional by the Supreme Court in 2024 after a petition by ADR.
 
 
 
• Electronic Voting Machines (EVMs)__
 
 
• A system used to record votes electronically in elections. ADR helped introduce a new system to verify EVMs after a judgment in 2024.

questions.question: The Grand Ethiopian Renaissance Dam (GERD) is located on which river?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Blue Nile River**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__**

__
 
• **The Grand Ethiopian Renaissance Dam (GERD) is located on the Blue Nile River in Ethiopia, about 30 km upstream from Sudan.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• **The GERD is Africa’s largest hydroelectric project, built for power generation and regional energy trade.**
 
• It is located on the Blue Nile River, which contributes around 85% of the water to the Nile River, making the project geopolitically sensitive.
 
• The dam has a height of about 170 meters and a length of approximately 2 km, with a reservoir capacity of 74 billion cubic meters.
 
• The dam’s power capacity ranges from 5,150 MW to 6,450 MW, making it the largest hydroelectric project in Africa.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• Blue Nile River__

 __
 
• One of the two major headstreams of the Nile River, providing around 70% of its floodwaters at Khartoum.
 
• It rises from a spring near Lake Tana in Ethiopia, flowing through rapids and gorges before joining the White Nile at Khartoum in Sudan.
 
 
 
• GERD Features__
 __
 
• Reservoir capacity: 74 billion cubic meters, flooding around 1,874 km².
 
• The dam aims to trap sediment inflow, ensuring sustainable power generation for decades.
 
 
 
• Nile River__
 
 
• The Nile River, formed by the confluence of the Blue Nile and White Nile, is crucial to the water security of Egypt and Sudan.

questions.question: Which country announced it will launch the world’s first nuclear power system with a closed fuel cycle by 2030?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Russia.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__**

__
 
• **President Vladimir Putin announced that Russia will launch the world’s first nuclear power system with a closed fuel cycle by 2030, aiming to reuse up to 95% of spent fuel.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• **The system will be built in the Tomsk Region and aims to drastically reduce radioactive waste and uranium demand.**
 
• **Russia invited international scientists to collaborate on testing at a new research centre in Ulyanovsk.**
 
• **The initiative emphasizes high safety standards, non-proliferation, and independent nuclear program development for other nations.**
 
• **The announcement was made at the World Atomic Week forum in Moscow, attended by global leaders including IAEA chief Rafael Grossi.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• Closed Fuel Cycle__

 __
 
• A closed fuel cycle in nuclear power reuses spent nuclear fuel, reducing radioactive waste and minimizing the need for fresh uranium.
 
 
 
• Tomsk Region__
 __
 
• The new nuclear power system will be constructed in Russia’s Tomsk Region, serving as a flagship project for advanced nuclear technology.
 
 
 
• Global Cooperation__
 __
 
• Russia encourages international collaboration and financing models to expand nuclear energy access worldwide while rejecting technological colonialism.
 
 
 
• IAEA and Safety Standards__
 
 
• The project aligns with high safety protocols and non-proliferation standards, ensuring responsible nuclear energy development.
